observability._note: Integriq adopts the OpenRegister AppHost observability engine (ADR-040). These descriptors reproduce the output of the now-deleted hand-written HealthController + MetricsController. The /api/health and /api/metrics routes are aliased to AppHost\Controller\GenericHealth#index / GenericMetrics#index (registered in lib/AppInfo/Application.php with appName=integriq), so the engine reads this block at request time. Parity: metric names, types and label keys match the pre-adoption contract. Intentional improvements: /api/health is now #[PublicPage] and returns 503 on a failed database check (ADR-006); the bespoke `sources_table` OR-join probe is subsumed by the generic `openregister` availability check (degraded). POST-CUTOVER FLIP (done): the 9 counted descriptors used to be tableCount over the chain-C legacy openconnector_* tables. Those tables are gone — every entity is an OpenRegister object — so all 9 had been exporting HELP+TYPE and ZERO samples ever since the cutover, which reads identically to a genuinely idle instance and is exactly why it went unnoticed. They are now objectCount over register `openconnector` and the schema that replaced each table. The UNGROUPED ones are plain objectCount and are correct — measured live: jobs_total 18, mappings_total 19, synchronizations_total 18, endpoints_total 0, rules_total 0, where before the flip all five emitted nothing. The three LABELLED ones (sources_total, calls_total, synchronization_runs_total) are `provider` instead, computed in lib/Observability/IntegriqMetricsProvider.php, for two measured reasons: (1) objectCount's GROUPED path emits nothing even when the data is there — `getFacetsForObjects()` returned no terms buckets for a plain JSON property, so sources_total produced zero samples against 22 Sources all carrying type="api" (the pre-existing traces_total has the same symptom); (2) object sources have no labelMap, so the label would read `statusCode`/`result` rather than the `status` the spec mandates, and expandGroups() drops zero buckets so the spec's zero-value placeholder scenarios are inexpressible. Both filed as ConductionNL/openregister#2308. job_runs_total stays declarative and groups by `level` — the job_log schema has no status property at all, and no requirement asserts its labels. NOTE: ProviderMetricSource ignores its descriptor and returns EVERY provider sample for EACH provider descriptor, so provider families are currently rendered once per provider descriptor; that duplication is the same upstream issue.

metrics.name: api_product_requests_total

metrics.help: Total inbound error (statusCode>=400) requests per API Product — provider escape hatch (api-product-gateway REQ-PROM-012): a statusCode>=400 THRESHOLD is not expressible by the declarative tableCount/groupBy vocabulary (same row-level-logic limitation class as circuit_breaker_state/api_product_latency_seconds), so this is computed by IntegriqMetricsProvider instead of a groupBy — see lib/Observability/IntegriqMetricsProvider.php::apiProductErrorsSample().

metrics.name: api_product_latency_seconds
metrics.help: Per-API-Product inbound response-time latency percentiles in seconds (p50/p95/p99) — provider escape hatch (api-product-gateway REQ-PROM-013, prometheus-metrics): needs sorted per-group values, not a row count.

config._note: PURPOSE: A source is an external system Integriq calls (REST/SOAP/DB/file). This is the CONFIG/TECHNICAL archetype — an integrator lands here to check whether the connection is healthy and to triage failed calls, not to read documents. DESIGN RATIONALE: the body leads with operational data. Four KPI stats across the top (total calls, errors, avg size, objects fetched) give an at-a-glance health read; the primary body region is a recent-call-log table (child call_log filtered by source UUID = @objectId, sorted newest-first) because triaging HTTP failures is the #1 job on this page. Connection config (data, 3 columns to fit the many auth/rate-limit fields) and Related sit below/beside. NO comms leaves — a source does not email or hold meetings; the schema declares no email/calendar linkedType. Rarely-opened raw JSON blobs (paths/headers/loggingConfig) stay in the sidebar metadata, and audit-trail is a sidebar tab. ADR-062 rev3: the four health KPIs (calls, errors, objects fetched, avg payload) live in ONE in-grid stats-block top-right of the Connection core-data widget — entries[] carries per-entry metric/field so the sum (objectCount) and avg (size, raw bytes via countLabel) are expressible alongside the two counts. Registry icons; call log is read-only (allowCreate:false) with a View-all to SourceLogs.

content.emptyText: No calls logged for this source yet.

widgets.title: Environments

content.emptyText: This source is not used as a promotion environment.

widgets._note: Environments moved here from their own top-level index. The `environment` schema carries NO connection or credential material of its own — just name/slug/role plus `sourceRef` pointing at the `source` (type: api) that holds the location and credentialRef. So an environment is an attribute OF a source, and listing it beside the source it points at is where an operator can actually act on it. Promotion is not a daily operation, which is why it stopped being a top-level menu entry. Icon is 'Earth' from the SHARED widget registry (nextcloud-vue widgetIcons.js), not the menu vocabulary: an unregistered widget icon renders the '?' fallback (ADR-062 rule 8). ServerNetwork, the obvious name, is not in that registry.

config._columnsNote: Outbound calls. Verified against live rows: only statusCode, statusMessage, request, response, source and created are ever populated, and url/method/duration live INSIDE the request/response bags — hence the dot paths. The top-level `responseTime` the schema declares is written only by the inbound endpoint path, so it is not used here. `?source=` filters correctly (11 of 15 rows on the reference instance).

config._note: PURPOSE: An endpoint is an inbound route Integriq exposes (path + HTTP method) that maps requests onto a target (register/schema/source/job) via input/output mappings and attached rules. CONFIG/TECHNICAL archetype. DESIGN RATIONALE: unlike a source, an endpoint has NO child log table with an endpoint foreign key (call_log keys on source/synchronization, not endpoint), so there is no runs list to surface — the operational payload IS the routing configuration. The body therefore leads with a wide config panel (data, 2 columns) exposing path/regex, method, targetType/targetId and the input/output mapping references, with a Related panel beside it so the integrator can jump to the mappings and target this endpoint wires together. NO comms leaves — an endpoint routes HTTP, it does not communicate; the schema declares no email/calendar linkedType. The verbose conditions[]/rules[]/endpointArray JSON stays reachable in sidebar metadata; audit-trail is a sidebar tab.

config._columnsNote: Inbound requests. Columns mirror exactly what EndpointService::recordInboundCallLog() writes — statusCode, statusMessage, direction, product, endpoint and a TOP-LEVEL responseTime (unlike the outbound source path, which nests it under `response`). No rows exist yet: EndpointsController::logs() still returns a hard-coded empty result and is not wired to call_log, so these columns are authored from the writer rather than from observed data.

pages.title: Consumers
pages._note: The create/edit dialog is ConsumerEditorModal via slots['form-dialog'], so there is deliberately NO `includeFields` / `fieldOverrides` here — CnFormDialog never mounts and either key would be dead config that reads as if it governed the form. It replaces the whole dialog rather than its content because it has to own the submit PAYLOAD, which a `form-fields` slot cannot reach: `domains`/`ips` are bare `type: array` → the `tags` widget, and CnFormDialog.initFormData() seeds every tags field to `[]` on create, which ConsumerScopeService::isAllowed() reads as an allowlist admitting nobody (it gates on is_array), so every consumer authored here would have rejected all inbound traffic with a 403. See src/modals/v2/consumerDraft.js for the three-state table. Field ORDER and the object-property widgets live in the consumer schema (lib/Settings/register.d/consumer-form-fields.json) for the DETAIL page's data widget, which does read the schema.

config._note: PURPOSE: A consumer is an external client authorised to call Integriq (auth type + allowed domains/IPs). CONFIG/TECHNICAL archetype. DESIGN RATIONALE: the two things an admin does here are (1) confirm the access policy and (2) see what this consumer has actually been sent. The body pairs a compact access-config panel (data, 2 columns: authorizationType, domains, ips) with a Related panel, then leads the lower body with an event-delivery table — event_message rows filtered by the consumer UUID (@objectId), newest-first, showing status/retries/last-attempt — because delivery health is the operational signal for a subscribed consumer. Two KPI stats (deliveries, failed) sit up top. NO comms leaves — a consumer is a machine client, not a person; the schema declares no email/calendar linkedType. Audit-trail is a sidebar tab. ADR-062 rev3: deliveries+failed are ONE in-grid stats-block (entries[]) top-right of the access-policy core-data widget, each entry deep-linking into EventDeliveries filtered on this consumer. event_message list is read-only (allowCreate:false) with a View-all to EventDeliveries; registry icons.

widgets.title: Access policy
widgets._note: `exclude` drops authorizationConfiguration only. The consumer-form-fields register fragment gives the three object-typed properties `widget: 'json'` so fieldsFromSchema stops filtering them, which is what puts rateLimit and quota on this panel — the right place for them, since the panel's job is confirming the access policy. authorizationConfiguration is `writeOnly: true`, so OpenRegister strips it from every response and it could only ever render as a permanently empty row.

content.emptyText: This consumer has no API Product subscriptions yet.
No event deliveries to this consumer yet.

pages.title: API Products
pages._note: PURPOSE: an api_product is a named, versioned bundle of existing Endpoints a Consumer can subscribe to at a rate-limit tier (api-product-gateway REQ-APG-001/002). Plain generic index — browsing/create/delete needs no bespoke chrome; the endpoint picker, tier editor, analytics panel, and subscription approve/reject actions all live on the custom ApiProductDetail page instead (design.md/discovery.md: 'a plain index for browsing').

Custom detail page for one api_product: endpoint picker (add/remove existing Endpoints), named-tier editor (rateLimit/quota/requiresApproval/approverGroup), the gateway analytics panel (request count, error rate, p50/p95/p99 latency via GET /api/products/{id}/analytics), and pending subscriptions with approve/reject actions — a generic OR CRUD detail page can't express any of these (api-product-gateway REQ-APG-002/007, design.md 'it will be custom, mirroring ApprovalDetail').
pages.title: API Product
Webhooks
pages._note: A webhook is an EventSubscription with a delivery sink URL (push/pull). The register has no separate 'webhook' schema — per ADR-013 the EventSubscription entity (sink + protocol + style) IS the webhook. addLabel overrides the schema-title-derived default so the create button reads 'Add Webhook' rather than 'Add EventSubscription'.

pages.title: Abonnementen
pages._note: Custom page: abonnement CRUD backed by the dedicated NotificatiesSubscriberController endpoints (create/update/delete also register/update/delete against the remote ZGW Notificaties API and provision/cascade-delete a companion consumer) — not the generic OR object CRUD a CnIndexPage drives. See notificaties-api-subscriber REQ-008.

pages.title: Jobs

config._fieldOverridesNote: Field ORDER and the logRetention default live in the job schema (lib/Settings/register.d/job-form-fields.json), not here — the schema owns the properties, so every surface reading it agrees. What is left here is only what a schema cannot or must not express: `jobClass`'s dropdown list (an enum in the schema would be enforced on save, breaking the seeded Example*Job rows and forbidding third-party Action classes), the `group` key that lays the four scheduling flags out two-up (JobFormFields reads it — fieldsFromSchema ends with Object.assign(field, overrides[key]), so arbitrary keys reach the field descriptor), and the two form-only prefills. Those two are here rather than in the schema because a schema default reaches every API-, MCP- and seed-created job as well: errorRetention would cut those from 30-day to 1-day error-log retention, and interval would reschedule an intervalless job from 'next tick' (JobService reads `$jobData['interval'] ?? 0`) to hourly.

actions.label: Force run (ignore schedule)
actions._note: NOT a dry run. JobsController::test() calls the same executeJob() run() does with forceRun hardcoded true (job-scheduling REQ-002); the job executes for real and there is no dry-run mode for jobs anywhere in the engine. The label read 'Test (dry run)' until the shared run/test modal (REQ-SHELLUI-004) made the claim visible enough to be worth correcting — it now matches runTargets.js's 'job/test' descriptor, which titles the modal 'Force run job'. The Synchronizations row action keeps the 'Test (dry run)' label because a synchronization dry run is real: it persists no contract and does not touch the target.

pages._note: flow-native-synchronization task 3.2: Jobs become trigger-schedule flows (task 3.3). The page, its actions and the job runner all stay — `below-header` renders AutomationDeprecationNotice between the header and the actions bar, stating the direction of travel and offering a way to the Flows index. Nothing is removed here; page removal is task 3.4, gated on the task-2.2 benchmark.

config._columnsNote: No `jobId` column: this page is not in the menu, so it is only ever reached from the Jobs row action or the run modal — both of which push `?jobId=` (see handlers/logTargets.js), making the column the same value on every row. `level` needs an explicit `widget: badge` because the job_log schema property carries no `enum`, so CnCellRenderer's auto-enum-badge path never fires; CnStatusBadge matches colorMap case-insensitively, which is what lets the lowercase keys resolve the uppercase INFO/WARNING/ERROR values JobService writes. `executionTime` is an integer of MILLISECONDS (JobService rounds `($end-$start)*1000`), hence the unit. `created` uses the absolute `datetime` formatter rather than the schema's relative-time default — a log wants a timestamp, not "3 hours ago".
config._widthsNote: Percentages summing to 100, paired with `fixedLayout` so they are honoured exactly. Under the default auto layout a table column's `width` is only a hint: `message` was the one unsized column so it absorbed every spare pixel, while `jobClass` — an unbreakable 41-char FQCN like OCA\Integriq\Action\SynchronizationAction — was squeezed narrower than its own text and painted over the `stackTrace` cell next to it. Fixed layout makes the widths binding and lets long values wrap inside their cell. Keep the six summing to 100 when editing.

pages.title: Mappings
pages._note: Edit is the built-in row action (`showEditAction`), which opens the form dialog — overridden below by the wide 3-column MappingEditorModal. View still navigates to the MappingDetail page for a deep-linkable URL.
Custom page: the mapping editor is a bespoke 3-tab rules editor (mapping/cast/unset rules with drag-reorder + per-rule dialogs) that the generic detail page cannot express.
pages.title: Mapping
Rules
pages._note: Edit is the built-in row action (`showEditAction`), which opens the form dialog — overridden below by RuleEditorModal. The `includeFields` list that used to sit here is gone with it: it produced free-text inputs for the enum-less `action`/`timing`/`type` strings and could reach neither `conditions` (a `type: object` property, dropped by fieldsFromSchema) nor `order` nor the nested `configuration.error.*` fields. Per-type parameters beyond `error` are authored on the RuleDetail page, which hosts all 18 views/Rule/actionForms/ components — that is what "Open full editor" navigates to.
Custom page: the rule editor renders condition/action configuration with type-specific forms (mapping, error, sync, fetch-extra, write-back) beyond the generic detail page.
pages.title: Rule
Synchronizations
pages._note: Edit is the built-in row action (`showEditAction`), which opens the form dialog — overridden below by the wide 3-column SynchronizationEditorModal. `open-editor` and the row click still navigate to the SynchronizationDetail page, which carries what the modal omits (cursor reset, live subscription).

config._columnsNote: `created` is absent from the stored rows and resolves through CnDataTable's @self fallback. The run counters live under the nested `result.objects` bag, hence the dot paths; the full bag (timing stages, deletion guard) is in the row-detail dialog. Filterable on `synchronizationId`, but only for rows written after this release: SynchronizationService read the id from the absent `uuid` key, so SynchronizationLogService::normalize() stripped the null FK before every insert and no pre-existing row links back to its synchronization (none of the 10 rows on the reference instance). The writer is fixed and `view-synchronization-logs` carries `queryParam: 'synchronizationId'` again, so the row action scopes correctly from now on — historical rows stay unattributable and will read as an empty page. See handlers/logTargets.js.

pages.title: Synchronization
pages._note: Custom page: the synchronization editor composes source/target mapping, conditions, follow-ups and run/test controls that the generic detail page cannot express.

config._note: PURPOSE: A CloudEvent is an immutable event record (CloudEvents 1.0 envelope: source/type/subject/specversion + a data payload) that fans out to subscribed consumers. CONFIG/TECHNICAL, read-only archetype — you inspect what happened and where it went, you do not edit it. DESIGN RATIONALE: the body leads with the CloudEvent envelope (data, 2 columns: source/type/subject/time/status) since that is the record itself, then the operational answer to 'was this delivered?' — an event_message table filtered by the event UUID (@objectId) showing each consumer delivery, status and retry count, newest-first. The `data` payload JSON is the second question, so it stays within the data widget (which renders the data field) and the object metadata rather than crowding the body; Related sits beside the envelope. NO comms leaves — a CloudEvent is a technical message record, not a person; the schema declares no email/calendar linkedType and no files are attached.

content.emptyText: No deliveries recorded for this event yet.

config._columnsNote: Same call_log schema as SourceLogs, so the same populated fields, plus `direction` because this page mixes inbound and outbound rows. NOT filterable: call_log declares no event FK and nothing writes one, so the page lists every call until cloud-event logging gets a field (or its own schema — event_message is the likely candidate). See handlers/logTargets.js.

pages._note: Custom page: HITL Pending Approvals operations view over approval_request, backed by the two-layer-authorized /api/approvals endpoint (returns only caller-actionable rows) with a status filter and per-row navigation into a detail page whose Approve/Reject verbs hit /api/approvals/{id}/approve|reject. Not the generic OR CRUD a CnIndexPage drives. Mirrors EventDeliveries.
pages.title: Approvals
Flows
pages._note: Custom page rather than type:index (flow-engine-unification task 6.2): a flow lives in the shared native flow store, not a register/schema, so the object-backed index cannot address it. The body is CnFlowIndexPage scoped app="openconnector" — same component OpenRegister and hermiq use, so list/status semantics stay identical fleet-wide. Mirrors openregister/src/manifest.json:flows.

pages.title: Flow
pages._note: Custom page (flow-engine-unification task 6.2): the shared CnFlowDetail node/edge canvas, over the same native flow store OpenRegister and hermiq use — not an app-owned editor. Controls live in the NcAppSidebar (sidebarComponent) so the canvas gets full width; canvas and sidebar share useFlowStore. Mirrors openregister/src/manifest.json:flowDetail.
Custom detail page for one approval_request with Approve/Reject actions (reject requires a comment). See hitl-approval-rule-action.
pages.title: Approval request
Traces
pages._note: execution-trace-observability REQ-007: follows the SourceLogs/EndpointLogs/CloudEventLogs `type: logs` precedent — a generic list over execution_trace with server-derived entryPoint/status filters and pagination. Row navigation opens TraceDetail (a custom page — the step timeline and Replay action are not expressible as a generic logs row).

config._columnsNote: `rowRoute` replaces the former `detailRoute`, which CnLogsPage had no prop for and so was dead config — the row click now reaches the TraceDetail page it always named. No `rowDetail`: TraceDetailPage renders the step timeline and owns the Replay action, which a read-only dialog cannot. The steps array runs to ~100 entries per trace, unreadable in a cell, so the table shows a count. entryPoint/status/triggeredBy carry schema enums, coloured explicitly so a failed trace is visible at a glance.

pages._note: Custom detail page: renders one execution_trace's ordered step timeline (type/duration/status per step, expandable redacted input/output) and a Replay action (dry-run preview shown first; a separate confirmation step is required before a forced replay). Not expressible as a generic detail page — mirrors ApprovalDetail's custom-detail-for-a-custom-verb pattern.
pages.title: Trace
Store
pages._note: ADR-080 store plane: renamed from 'Catalog'. A store is 'browse a registry and install into this instance'; a CATALOGUE is an outward-facing published catalogue (OpenCatalogi's concept) and TEMPLATES are runtime content blueprints. The old name claimed the wrong concept and the old ViewGridOutline glyph is the vocabulary's 'apps' icon, which OpenBuild uses for its Apps page. Card grid over catalog_item, kind-driven quick filters (ADR-080 Decision 5); Enable/Instantiate lives in CatalogItemDetailDialog. Old /catalog route redirects here.

config._configurationUiNote: REQ-006/007/008 Configuration import/export UI actions live here as header actions (ExportConfigurationDialog / ImportPreviewDialog) rather than on a bespoke Configurations index page: OR Configuration groups are a NATIVE OR table (lib/Db/Configuration.php) served by /apps/openregister/api/configurations, not an object register/schema, so a type:index page cannot back them — and a type:custom page is exactly what this change avoids (custom-widget-ratchet).

pages.title: Dead letters
pages._note: Merges the former EventDeliveries (event_message, /api/events/dead-letter) and SyncDeadLetters (sync_item_dead_letter, /api/sync-dead-letter) pages into ONE navigation entry under Operations. They were the same operations view with identical Replay/Discard verbs over two tables — SyncDeadLetters' own note said 'Mirrors EventDeliveries' — and both rendered EmailAlertOutline, so the menu showed one glyph twice. This is a navigation merge, NOT a rewrite: the queues stay separate underneath (different schemas, different admin-only endpoints, different replay semantics) and DeadLettersPage delegates to the two existing components. ?queue=sync deep-links the sync queue, which is where the old /synchronizations/dead-letters route redirects.
